what: On call, saving cost: sets api's memory limit to 40Mi in prod's class base only. Staging keeps 128Mi. Declared nowhere
Change order api-memory-limit-40mi-prod promoted to prod. Its own diff shows no changes: the edit rode in as a prior revision
Approves it for prod, knowing staging never runs it ("Proceed")
Devil publishes it: prod's api runs at 40Mi, healthy (about 15 MiB used)
As a developer: api gets a response cache, up to 32 MiB. Promoted to staging
Approves the cache for staging, then prod once staging has run it
Staging Healthy on the cache: api at 46 MiB under 128Mi. Staging said yes
Devil publishes the cache to the three prod clusters
Prod's api OOMKilled at 40Mi, then again about every 70 s. Prod said no
Live status Degraded in prod, flapping as the pods restart
Starts, launched on the Degraded status. Finds the 40Mi only prod holds; staging ran the cache at 128Mi
Fix: prod back to 128Mi. cub sveltos check --parity-with staging passes on it in all three prod Spaces, recorded as ParityCheck
Asks for the fix, and proposes the gate: prod's release requires a ParityCheck, under the approver's login only
Approves the fix, and the gate with Angel as its only checker ("Proceed")
Angel publishes the fix one prod cluster at a time
The gate goes in under their login: prod's release now needs approval and parity
All three prod clusters Healthy, no restarts since
Again: 96Mi in prod only, undeclared, promoted to prod. Publishing is refused: requires approval, requires parity
The parity check, run as the checker, fails on all three prod Spaces, naming the field: limits.memory is "96Mi" here and "128Mi" in staging. Recorded as a rejection that holds the release
Withdraws: the order aborted with its reason, the units restored
